fixture: by-links-3d, a 3D default layout: each case's input and the answer the reference implementation gives
call: the layout of the graph { nodes: input.nodes, edges: input.edges } with input.rows as the world's elements, at `steps` force steps (300, the method's own count, in every case); input.held and input.heldUnit are handed only where the input has the key (a null is handed as null). The answer also carries the method's word, `by-links-3d` (step 12): no case's want holds it, and a checker compares it on every case that answers (a refusal answers nothing)
rows: input.rows is the world's Map, Pin, Marker and Zone elements as served (only the keys the map-space profile and its layout reading read), or null. They are read as the map-space profile reads them, and its layout reading says which Map is a layout map; the method has no reading of its own
table: table_sha256 is the sha256 of the directions table the method reads (layout-by-links-3d.directions.json), the same bytes in every implementation
unplaced_order: by id: the ids of the nodes not placed, in code point order; the same order as the flat methods' unplaced and the saved Map's reading

compare.pieces: each case's graph read into pieces (step 10: the undirected pairs, a link whose end is no node passed over, a self-link none; the main piece the largest, a tie to the smaller least id in code point order); a ring piece is every other piece of two nodes or more with no node pinned (want.how "map") and no node held (in input.held and not pinned)
compare.exact: every ids, unplaced, how, group, part, held and centres entry; and every element not of a ring piece whose how is centre, with or map, or whose want.held is true: each of x, y, z the same double, a zero compared by its value (JSON writes no -0)
compare.within: every element whose how is arm or link and whose held is false, and every coordinate of every element of a ring piece (z included): each within 1e-9 of a rest (6e-8 units), because those are placed with the runtime's cosine and sine (the ring's angles and its arcsine too)
compare.held: every element whose want.held is true, whatever its how: each of x, y, z the same double as input.held gives for it (it stands at its held point)
compare.refused: a case whose want is { refused: code }: the call throws and answers nothing, and the error carries that code (in JavaScript err.code, on a TypeError for held-not-object and held-not-point, a RangeError for held-box and held-unit); held-not-object, held-not-point and held-unit are read before anything runs, held-box by each run on the held points it holds, the main run first, then the ring order
compare.fit: a piece joins a ring while the angles summed so far on it plus its own are at most 2 pi - fit; a verdict whose sum lies within fit_band of 2 pi - fit is promised either ring, and no case here holds one: every fit sum of every case (as the checker's own run sums them) stands more than fit_band from 2 pi - fit
compare.unplaced: exact: the same ids in the same order

held: a case named "held: ..." hands back points the method answered for an earlier input (input.held, element id to [x, y, z]; with input.heldUnit where the points were rounded)
points: want.points is x, y, z of each placed element in want.ids order (the order input.nodes was handed in, the nodes not placed left out), 3 numbers an element
unplaced: `unplaced`, after the cases: for each case, the id of every node of graph.nodes that is not in placed, in code point order (the reading of a saved Map: a node it holds no Pin for). A member of placed that is not a non-empty string is passed over; a placed id that is no node is no part of the answer

cases.name: nothing
cases.why: No nodes, and one edge whose ends are no nodes: the edge is passed over and the answer is empty, every list empty and no centres (step 1; step 12).

cases.name: two linked
cases.why: Two linked elements, handed as b then a: no node has three neighbours (least is never under 3), so none is taken and the first node of the ranking is the one centre, a, the lower node among equal counts; the answer's rows keep the handed order, b first (step 3, the pick; step 12).

cases.name: a self-link
cases.why: A self-link makes no pair: d, linked to a and to itself, has one neighbour, so at depth 1 with degree 1 it hangs from a as a link (step 1; step 9, what hangs).

cases.name: one body with no arm
cases.why: A wheel of six round h: every element is in the body, h is the one centre, nothing hangs and nothing is off; only the six movers that are not fixed count in the group's ball (step 7, free and ball).

cases.name: an arm three links long
cases.why: An arm r (depth 1), q (2), p (3) hangs from c: the list is by depth, then the one order, so r takes place 0 though p comes first in the one order; r has two neighbours, so every member is an arm, with group null and part one-link (step 9, what hangs; step 12).

cases.name: two largest blocks of one size
cases.why: Two cycles of four sharing a (a b c e and a d f g): read member by member in rising order, the blocks first differ at b against d, so a d f g is the body, and b, c and e hang from a (step 2, the blocks).

cases.name: two largest blocks of one size, the body closed first
cases.why: Two cycles of four sharing d (a b c d and d e f g): the body is the block with the higher node at the first difference, d e f g, though a depth-first walk from a closes it first and a b c d last; a, b and c hang from d. The case above cannot tell this rule from taking the block the walk closes last: there both give a d f g (step 2, the blocks).

cases.name: a small group gives its centre up
cases.why: A ring of nine with chords: the pick takes e02, e01 and e05; e01's group holds two, under MIN_GROUP, so e01 is no centre any more and reach is read again, leaving e02 and e05 (step 3, the pick).

cases.name: a hub linked to a third of the rest
cases.why: A ring of ten whose hub e00 is linked to four of the other nine: e00 alone is taken, its group is the whole body (twice its members more than the body's size), so the pick runs again on its members without e00, and three new centres, e02, e05 and e07, are added after it (step 3, the centres).

cases.name: path counts past 2^52
cases.why: The layer x0 to x7 stands 19 links from the centres h1 and h2, which reach it by 2^54 and 9 * 8^17 shortest paths; each count is capped at WAYS_CAP (2^52), so the counts are equal, the tie goes to the lower rank and the layer joins h1, where exact counts would give h2 (step 3, reach).

cases.name: a Map that holds two
cases.why: A Map with Pins on only two elements of the graph: the first map has fewer than three elements, so there is no plate and no element is placed map (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Map that holds three
cases.why: Three elements pinned on one Map make the plate: each stands at the plate's point plus ((x - W / 2) * scale, (y - H / 2) * scale, 0); b4, a pinned centre, keeps its group, which stands over the plate (step 4, its places; step 5, the points; step 12); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a small plate over a place
cases.why: m2 stands at b4, a place on the first map m1, and holds r1, r2 and f1: they stand round b4 at m2's own scale sc and REST * 2 above it, r2, at m2's middle, straight over b4 (step 4, the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a small plate taken on the second pass
cases.why: m2 stands at r2, which only m3 places, and m2 comes first by id: the first pass passes m2 over and takes m3, and a second pass takes m2, whose elements stand REST * 2 above r2 (step 4, the small plates: passes until a pass takes none); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their Pins and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: two Maps tied for first
cases.why: m1 and m2 each hold three elements: the tie goes to the greater id, so m2 is the first map and b3, b5 and b7 stand on the plate (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: an element pinned twice on one map
cases.why: b2 has two Pins on m1, p-b at (90, 90) handed first and p-a at (10, 10): the Pins are walked by pin id and an element keeps the first place it was given, so b2 stands at p-a's (step 4, the pins); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a saved layout Map beside a real Map
cases.why: lay, a Map whose x_layout is {"method": "by-kind"}, holds a Pin for every element but is a layout map, so it is none of step 4's maps and the plate is m1's, the real Map of three (step 4, the maps; the map-space profile's rules 8 and 11); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: the only Map is a layout map
cases.why: The world's one Map is a layout map holding a Pin for every element: it is left out, so there is no plate and no element is placed map (step 4, the maps; the map-space profile's rule 11: a world whose every Map is a layout map has no Map for its space); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a layout map over a place on the plate
cases.why: lay2 stands at b4, a place on the first map m1, and holds three elements with no place yet, but it is a layout map, so it is no small plate and r1, r2 and f1 stay off the map (step 4, the maps and the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: the neighbours of the layout mark
cases.why: Five Maps whose x_layout is null (m1), an array (m2), {"method": ""} (m3), {"method": 5} (m4) and {} (m5) carry no layout mark, so all five are maps: m1 is the first map and m2 to m5 are small plates over b4, b6, b8 and b2 (step 4, the maps; the map-space profile's rule 8: a layout map's method is a non-empty string); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their Pins and not moved (step 10).

cases.name: a Pin with one link key
cases.why: b8's Pin has an element_id and no element_type: the map-space profile's reading answers a Pin's element only when it carries both, so b8 is not on the plate, which is made from the other three (the map-space profile's reading; step 4, the pins); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: Pins that are no point
cases.why: b8's Pin has x 40.5 and b3's has x true: a Pin without a whole x and y is no point in the map-space profile's reading, so neither element is on the plate (the map-space profile's reading; step 4, the pins); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Map with no width or height
cases.why: m1 has no width and no height: the map-space profile's reading gives each as the largest x and y among the Map's own points (80 and 90), so the plate is made in that frame (step 4, the first map; the map-space profile's rule 2); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a first Map with a width of 0
cases.why: m1 holds four elements and is the first map, and its own width is 0: that is not a number over 0, so there is no plate, and m2, which holds three and has a size, is not tried in its stead (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a first Map with a width under 0
cases.why: m1's own width is -100, a whole number the standard allows and the map-space profile's reading answers as written: it is not over 0, so there is no plate and nothing is refused, and m2 is not tried in its stead (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a first Map with a width and a height under 0
cases.why: m1's width and height are both -100: W * H is over 0, so only the rule that each be a number over 0 keeps m1 from being a plate with every place mirrored (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a small Map with a width and a height under 0
cases.why: m2 stands at b4, a place on the plate, and holds three new elements, but its width and height are -60 and -40, not over 0: it is not taken, and r1, r2 and f1 stay off the map (step 4, the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: two Pin rows with one id
cases.why: Two rows carry the Pin id p01, the first for b2 and the later for b3: the map-space profile's reading takes the last row served for an id, so b3 is on the plate and b2 is not (the map-space profile's reading; step 4, the pins); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Map whose location is no id
cases.why: m2's location is a list, ["b4"]: an id is a non-empty string, so the map-space profile's reading gives m2 no location; it stands at no place, is no small plate, and r1, r2 and f1 stay off the map (the map-space profile's reading; step 4, the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Map id served twice, the later row a layout map
cases.why: Two rows carry the Map id m1, the first a plain Map and the later a layout map: the last row served is the element, so m1 is a layout map, the world has no Map for its space and there is no plate (the map-space profile's reading and its rule 11; step 4, the maps); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Map id served twice, the earlier row a layout map
cases.why: Two rows carry the Map id m1, the first a layout map and the later a plain Map: the last row served is the element, so m1 is a map and makes the plate (the map-space profile's reading; step 4, the maps); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: Moppetopia
cases.why: A world with a map, its graph and its Maps and Pins as a stranger is served them: every step at once, the plate included (steps 1 to 12); and under the pieces, 30 nodes are not placed (step 12).

nodes.name: What Happened in the Moistened Valley
The Gift of the Left Eye
What the Left Eye Sees at Night
The Left Eye at the Year Zero Reading
Cadet Fluffington's Assessment of Cadet Snoot
We Sail Where the Puddles Flow
First Eternal Drip Pressure Drop Recorded

cases.name: Blood Meridian, the graph alone
cases.why: A world's graph handed with no Maps or Pins, so no plate: every step but the plate (steps 1 to 12; step 4 gives no plate); and under the pieces, 9 nodes are not placed (step 12).

nodes.name: Government of the State of Chihuahua
Government of the State of Sonora
Signing of the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
The gold rush on the southern road
The killings at the Yuma Crossing
The Comanche attack on White's company
The country, read as a stranger
Tongues he has not heard before
The tavernkeeper’s wife and the kid

cases.name: held: the whole answer handed back
cases.why: The answer of this same input handed back whole, a plate and a small plate in it: the same answer to the bit. The frame is found from the four held places on m1, and each pinned element, its standing place within band of its held point, stands at that held point, with held false (H1; H4; H6, kept); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their Pins and not moved (step 10), and s2 is not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a leaf added to a held arm
cases.why: r0, new, hangs from b3 beside the held arm r1 (depth 1, place 0) and r2 (depth 2, place 1): a place is claimed at the kept node's own depth, so r0 takes place 2, though place 1 at r0's depth is near no kept node; every old point is unchanged (H6, what hangs); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a leaf beside a held leaf under a pinned parent
cases.why: f1 hangs from b5, which is pinned, and is held at place 0; f0, new, takes place 1, a quarter of a rest away (fan * 0.5 for a pinned cut): LINE is an eighth of a rest, so the held leaf claims its own place and no other (H6, what hangs); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: an element added to the body
cases.why: b9, new, is linked to b8 and b2 and joins the body; the centres are read from today's graph (b1, b8) and every old point is unchanged, the kept nodes outside the body (the arm and the link) standing in the force steps as fixed movers that push and are not moved, and the kept body nodes fixed at their held points (H5; Held points: steps 1 to 3 do not change); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a Pin added on the first map
cases.why: b3 gets a Pin on m1 and the earlier answer is handed back: the frame is found from the held places of the four elements m1 held before (b3's held point, a place in the body, does not agree), so the plate keeps the earlier scale and point though m1 now holds five, no other pinned element moves, and b3 stands at its Pin (H1; H4); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: an earlier answer rounded to whole numbers, with heldUnit
cases.why: The earlier answer rounded to whole numbers, handed back with heldUnit 1 and a new Pin for b3: band is 3 * heldUnit + SNAP, so the frame is found within three units of the rounded places, and every earlier element stands at its rounded point exactly, the pinned ones by the snap (H1; H4); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: an earlier answer rounded to whole numbers, with no heldUnit
cases.why: The same hand-back with heldUnit left out: band is SNAP alone, a billionth of a rest, and the rounded places agree with no frame, so step 4 stands, the plate is packed as a free part beside the fixed groups, and the four pinned elements held before move (H1, with none; H3); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: two places of the map handed back
cases.why: Everything handed back but b6 and b8, two of the four elements on m1: two candidates cannot reach FRAME_AGREE (3), so there is no frame, the plate is packed as a free part and its four elements move (H1; H3); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a centre not handed back
cases.why: Everything handed back but the centre b7: its group's point is the mean of its held members b6 and b8 and its part is fixed there, and b7 is not fixed: it starts in its group's ball and moves as any member (H2 case 3; H5); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a centre not handed back, three members held
cases.why: Everything handed back but the centre b4, whose group keeps three held members (b2, b3, b5): the group's point is their mean, each of x, y and z added in the one order and divided by three. A sum of three doubles shows its order in the last place, where a sum of two (the case above) cannot (H2 case 3); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a new centre beside held ones
cases.why: A wheel of seven, new, joined to b7 and b8: its hub n0 is a centre nobody held, so its group's part is placed by the packing beside the fixed ones, and n0 is not fixed in the steps; every old point is unchanged (H2 case 4; H3; H5); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a link added, a piece joins
cases.why: A link from q1 to b8 joins the piece q1, q2 to the main piece: both now hang from b8 as arms, and both are kept, so they stand at their held points with the how their new rule gives, and no element moves (H6, kept); and under the pieces, s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a link added, the centres change
cases.why: A link from f1 to b6 puts f1 in the body, and today's centres are b1, b6 and b7 (b4 no longer one): the centres and each element's group are today's, and no element moves, since every one is held (Held points: steps 1 to 3 do not change; H6, kept); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: null, and heldUnit null
cases.why: held null and heldUnit null are read as absent: the method's own answer, bit for bit, and held false for every element (Held points; step 12); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: only an id that is no node
cases.why: A held id that is no node is passed over, and when no held id is a node the method runs as written, to the bit (Held points); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a box exactly 768 rests wide
cases.why: b1 and b2 held 46,080 units apart on x, exactly HELD_BOX * REST: only more than that is refused, so both stand at their held points (Refused); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: heldUnit exactly an eighth of a rest
cases.why: heldUnit 7.5 is LINE itself, and both ends are allowed: it is taken, and only a larger one is refused (Refused); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: refused: held is an array
cases.why: held is an array, not a mapping of element ids to points: it is refused with held-not-object before anything else is read (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a held point of two numbers
cases.why: A held value of two numbers: a value must be exactly three finite numbers, so held-not-point (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a held point of four numbers
cases.why: A held value of four numbers: exactly three, so a fourth number is not passed over and the value is refused with held-not-point (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a held point with a string in it
cases.why: A held value with the string "3" in it: a string is no number and nothing is converted, so held-not-point (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a bad point under an id that is no node
cases.why: A value of two numbers under zz, an id that is no node: every value is read before any id is passed over, so it is refused with held-not-point (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a box one unit wider than 768 rests
cases.why: b1 and b2 held 46,081 units apart on x: more than HELD_BOX * REST apart, so held-box (Refused).

cases.name: held: an id that is no node widens no box
cases.why: b1 at (0, 0, 0) and zz, an id that is no node, 46,081 units away on y: zz enters no run, so it is in no run's box and the call is answered, b1 standing at its held point (Refused); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: refused: heldUnit over an eighth of a rest
cases.why: heldUnit 7.6 is over LINE (7.5), so held-unit (Refused).

cases.name: refused: heldUnit a string
cases.why: heldUnit given as the string "1": it is no finite number and nothing is converted, so held-unit (Refused).

cases.name: refused: heldUnit under 0 with nothing held
cases.why: heldUnit -1 with no held at all: heldUnit is read whether or not anything is held, and under 0 it is refused with held-unit (Refused).

cases.name: two small groups at once
cases.why: A ring of eight (e00 to e07) with the chords e01-e03 and e04-e07: the pick takes e01, e04 and e07, and the groups of e04 and of e07 hold two each, both under MIN_GROUP at once. The one taken last, e07, is no centre any more; with reach read again e04's group holds four and keeps its centre (step 3, the pick).

cases.name: one rivals link, one way
cases.why: The fifteen-element graph of the cases above with one rivals link more, from b8 (in b7's group, part 2) to b1 (part 0), on a pair already linked: opp counts it whichever end is the source, so the ends are parts 0 and 2, where the links alone would choose parts 1 and 2 (step 5, the counts and the directions); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: ids on either side of U+FFFF
cases.why: Two linked elements whose ids differ in their second character, U+FF21 and U+10000: in the one order, by code point, the U+FF21 id comes first and is the centre, where UTF-16 units (U+10000 is D800 DC00) would put the other first. The other is the one mover not fixed, and its start number h is worked out over its id's UTF-8 bytes, four of them for U+10000 (step 1; step 3, the pick; step 7).

cases.name: held: one part, and it is fixed
cases.why: A wheel of six round h is one group, so one part, and h is held at (100, 50, -30): the group's point is that held point and the one part is fixed there, not at (0, 0, 0), and the wheel settles round it (H2 case 2; H3; step 5, the packing).

cases.name: held: a pinned element that hangs takes a place
cases.why: r1 hangs from b3 and is pinned on m1; the earlier answer is handed back whole and r3, new, hangs from b3 too. b3's list is r1 and r3 (depth 1, in the one order), then r2 (depth 2, kept), whose held point claims place 1; r1, pinned, takes the lowest free place, 0, and then stands at its Pin, so r3 takes place 2; every old point is unchanged (H6, what hangs); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: the fan when u points straight down
cases.why: c and m are the body, c its centre held at (0, 0, 0) and m held at (0, 0, 60), and two new leaves, l1 and l2, hang from c: the group's point is c's held point, so u from it to c is zero and outward is the way from the middle to the group's point, straight down; u × (0, 0, 1) is zero, so t is u × (1, 0, 0), and l2, at place 1, is the first leaf whose point reads t. m's id comes after l2's, so the block c m is the body and not c l2 (H2 case 2; step 9, outward and what hangs; step 2, the blocks).

cases.name: a small plate of twenty
cases.why: m1, the first map, holds b4 and k01 to k20; m2 stands at b4 and holds k02 to k20, placed already, and k21: twenty elements, those with a place counted, so its one new element stands REST * 4 above b4, not REST * 2 (step 4, the small plates: the rise); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a partner held at the mirror of its place
cases.why: a, b and c are held and on m1, b at the mirror of its frame place about a (as far from a, the other way in x and in y): the pair a, b gives s = 2 and F = (1000, 500, 40), where a and c agree and b, tested as every candidate is, lies outside band, so the pair counts two, no other pair reaches FRAME_AGREE, there is no frame, and the plate is packed as a free part beside the held wheel, a, b and c away from their held points (H1, with none; H3).

cases.name: the largest group read again twice
cases.why: A body of thirteen whose pick takes one centre, v01, so its group has more than half the body: picked again without v01 it gives v04 and v09, with seven and five members, and v01 keeps itself alone; v04's seven are still more than half of thirteen, so its group is picked again a second time, adding v06 and v07 with three members each, and the centres are five (step 3, the centres, at most twice).

cases.name: a group of exactly half the body
cases.why: A body of fourteen whose pick takes v02, v03 and v12, with seven, three and four members: twice v02's seven is fourteen, not more than the body's size, so no group is picked again and the centres stay three (step 3, the centres).

cases.name: two pairs of parts tied on opposing links
cases.why: Eight nodes in three parts of sizes 1, 4 and 3 (v00 keeps itself alone when its group is picked again): opp(0, 2) and opp(1, 2) are 1 and opp(0, 1) is 0, so the greatest opp is a tie, and the greater size(p) + size(q), 7 against 4, makes parts 1 and 2 the ends (step 5, the directions).

cases.name: five parts, the ends among the four largest
cases.why: Sixteen nodes in five parts of sizes 1, 4, 3, 5 and 3 and no opp: the ends are read among the four parts of greatest size, 1 to 4, where link(1, 4) is 0 and parts 1 and 4 stand; part 0, the smallest, is not read, though link(0, 1) is 0 too and, read first, it would stand (step 5, the directions).

cases.name: an opposing link weighed four times
cases.why: Eleven nodes in four parts of sizes 1, 4, 3 and 3, with opp 1 between parts 0 and 2, 1 and 2, and 1 and 3: the ends are parts 1 and 2, and part 3 chooses between directions 1 and 2 with link(1, 3) - 4 * opp(1, 3) = -2 against part 1 and link(2, 3) = 1 toward part 2, so it takes direction 2, where weighing opp once would give 1 and direction 1 (step 5, the directions and cost).

cases.name: a pinned element outside the body counted in the plate
cases.why: m1 pins v01, v03, v05 and v09 of the body and v07, which hangs outside it; v03 is a pinned centre, so its group stands over the plate, and the parts are v00's group (size 2), v04's (3) and the plate (5, v07 counted). With no opp the ends are parts 1 and 2, link 2 against sizes 3 and 5, before parts 0 and 1, link 1 against sizes 2 and 3; with the plate's size 4, without v07, the two pairs tie and parts 0 and 1, read first, would stand (step 5, the counts and the directions).

cases.name: refused: a bad point, a box too wide and a bad heldUnit at once
cases.why: held has a value of two numbers (b1) and points 46,081 units apart on x (b2 and b3), and heldUnit is -1: three refusals apply, and the first in their order, held-not-point, is the one (Refused).

cases.name: refused: a held point with true in it
cases.why: b1 is held at [true, 0, 0]: a boolean is no number, so the value is not exactly three finite numbers and is refused with held-not-point, though a language whose true is the number 1 would read (1, 0, 0) (Refused).

cases.name: refused: heldUnit true
cases.why: heldUnit is true, with b1 held at (0, 0, 0): a boolean is no number, so heldUnit is refused with held-unit, though a language whose true is the number 1 would read it as 1 (Refused).

cases.name: thirteen hubs over the floor, twelve centres
cases.why: Thirteen hubs w00 to w12 in a ring, each with a rim of ten, one block of 143 nodes: each hub's count is 12 and least is 12, and no hub has more than one neighbour that is a centre taken before it or that centre's neighbour (2 * 1 < 12), so every hub passes, and the walk stops when MAX_CENTRES are taken: w12 is no centre and joins w00 (step 3, the pick and reach).

cases.name: a link to an id that is no node
cases.why: d hangs from a and has one edge more, to zz, which is no node: that edge is passed over, so d has one neighbour and, at depth 1 with degree 1, is placed link (step 1; step 9, what hangs).

cases.name: a Pin naming an id that is no node
cases.why: m1 has whole Pins for b2, b4 and zz, and m1 is one of the maps, but zz is no node, so its Pin does not count: m1 has two elements, fewer than three, and there is no plate (step 4, the pins and the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a small Map that holds two
cases.why: m2 stands at b4, which has a place on m1, its width and height are numbers over 0, and it holds r1 and r2, neither placed: two elements are fewer than three, so m2 is not taken and r1 and r2 are not pinned (step 4, the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a partner held at the same x and y
cases.why: a to e are held and on the first map, and b and e are held at a's own point. a's partners by map distance, greatest first, begin with b, whose held x and y are a's, so the next is tried, c: s = 2 and F = (1000, 500, 40), where a, c and d agree, FRAME_AGREE of them, and that is the frame; b and e stand at their places on the plate, far from their held point (H1; H4).

cases.name: a rivals link to a pinned element outside the body
cases.why: r1 hangs from b3 and is pinned on m1 with b2 and b8, and an edge with the field rivals runs from b3 to r1 beside their friends link: r1 is outside the body, so that edge counts in no opp, though r1 counts in the plate part's size; every opp is 0 and the ends are read from link (step 5, the counts and the directions); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a plate with no link to the body
cases.why: A triangle a, b, c is the body and one group, and x, y and z, with no edge, are pinned on m1: the group and the plate are two parts, link(0, 1) is 0, so total is 0 and is read as 1; the two parts start further apart than GAP * (r[0] + r[1]), so f is over 0 and is multiplied by 0.02 + 0.5 * 0 / 1 (step 5, the packing).

cases.name: held: the group's point at the middle of the body
cases.why: A triangle c, e1, e2 held at (0, 0, 0), (60, 0, 0) and (-60, 0, 0), and l, new, hanging from e1: the centre c is held, so cpt is (0, 0, 0) (H2, case 2), and the middle is (0, 0, 0) too, so o has no length and is (0, 0, 1); l, at place 0, stands at cpt + u * (skin + REST) with u = (1, 0, 0) + 0.75 * (0, 0, 1) divided by its length: (96, 0, 72) (step 9, outward and what hangs).

cases.name: a Pin row whose id is empty
cases.why: b8's Pin row has the id "": the map-space reading reads a row without a non-empty string id as no element, so b8 has no Pin and the first map holds b2, b4 and b6 (What it reads besides the graph; step 4); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Pin whose map is a number
cases.why: The Map "7" has Pins for b2 and b4, and b6's Pin names its map by the number 7: an id is a string, so the map-space reading serves that Pin no Map, "7" has two elements, and there is no plate (What it reads besides the graph; step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Marker measuring a Map
cases.why: m1 has no width and no height, its Pins reach x 80 and y 90, and a Marker of the served zone z1 on m1 stands at (95, 95): the map-space reading measures a Map from its own placed Markers and Pins (its rule 2), so W and H are 95 (What it reads besides the graph; step 4, its places); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a Marker of a zone that is not served
cases.why: m1 has no width and no height, its Pins reach x 80 and y 90, and a Marker on m1 at (95, 95) names the zone z9, which is not served: the map-space reading places no such Marker (its rule 4), so it measures nothing, and W and H are 80 and 90 (What it reads besides the graph; step 4, its places); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a first Map with a height of 0
cases.why: m1 holds four elements, its width is 100 and its height 0: the height is not a number over 0, so there is no plate, though the width is one (step 4, the first map); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: a small Map with a height of 0
cases.why: m2 stands at b4, which has a place on m1, and holds r1, r2 and f1, none placed; its width is 60 and its height 0, not a number over 0, so it is not taken and the three are not pinned (step 4, the small plates); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 stand on the ring (steps 10 and 11), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a linked point 1e-7 from a moving element's start (the links' floor)
cases.why: A wheel of six round h, h held at (0, 0, 0), and n1 held 1e-7 to the side of where n2 starts (step 7): n1 is kept and fixed (H5), and n1 and n2 are a link, at step 0 1e-7 apart, so d is max(length(u), 0.000001) = 0.000001 (step 8, the links).

cases.name: held: a fixed part 1e-7 from a free part's start (the packing's floor)
cases.why: The body of fourteen whose centres are v02, v03 and v12: v02 and v03 are held, so their parts are fixed at their held points (H2, case 2), and v12's part starts at O + dir * sum (H3); v03 is held at twice v12's dir times sum, 2e-7 further on x, so O is half that and v12's part starts 1e-7 from v03's, and dist is max(length(d), 0.000001) = 0.000001 (step 5, the packing; H3).

cases.name: pieces: two equal pieces
cases.why: Two triangles of one size: the main piece is the one that holds the lower node (a, e, f), and the other is laid out by its own links in a run of its own and stands on the ring beside it (steps 2 and 10; step 11).

cases.name: pieces: no link at all
cases.why: Four nodes and no link: every piece is one node and none is pinned, so nothing is placed, centres is empty and unplaced lists all four by id (steps 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: one node
cases.why: One node and no link: it is not placed, and the main run's centre, that node, is left out of centres (steps 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: a main and three equal pieces
cases.why: A wheel of sixteen and three loops of ten of one shape: all three stand on the first ring in the order of their lowest nodes, C0, D0 and E0, each at its own angle, and the ring's radius is read from rmax over every ring piece, so the widest, E0, though last, is as far from the main shape as the others (step 11).

cases.name: pieces: a star, a star piece and a chain
cases.why: A star of fifteen as the main piece, a star of ten and a chain of nine: the chain has fewer nodes and comes second in the order, but it is the wider piece, and the first ring stands rmax plus RING_GAP out from the main shape with rmax the chain's (step 11).

cases.name: pieces: the fit margin, rings of five and one
cases.why: A main pair held 84.69017955578292 apart and six free pairs: the sixth's angles sum to 5e-7 rad under 2 * PI, so it would join at 2 * PI and does not at 2 * PI - FIT, standing five FIT_BAND from that edge, and the rings hold five and one (step 11, the fit test).

cases.name: pieces: a chain pinned at both ends
cases.why: A chain P00 to P05 pinned at both ends, beside a wheel with two Pins: its run holds P00 and P05 at their Pins, and the piece is laid out round those points and not moved (step 10).

cases.name: pieces: a loop pinned at two places
cases.why: A loop of eight pinned at P0 and P4, beside a wheel with two Pins: its run holds both at their Pins, and the piece is laid out round those points and not moved (step 10).

cases.name: pieces: a piece with two held nodes
cases.why: A chain of six with H01 and H03 held: its run holds them at their held points, and the piece is laid out round them and not moved, both standing at their held points, held true (step 10; H5).

cases.name: pieces: all in one
cases.why: A wheel with two Pins, a piece with two Pins, a chain with two held nodes, two loops of ten and seven pairs on the ring, and three nodes with no link: each case of step 10 at once, the ring of step 11 of nine pieces, and unplaced a0, z1, z2 by id (steps 10 to 12).

cases.name: pieces: three rings
cases.why: A main pair and eighteen pairs, the smallest such world that makes three rings: the rings hold five, twelve and one, each next one 2 * rmax + RING_GAP further out (step 11).

cases.name: pieces: a pinned lone node beside an unpinned one
cases.why: Two nodes with no link: L1 has a Pin on the Map with W01 and W05 and stands at its place there, how map, and L2 has none and is in unplaced (steps 4, 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: a held lone node is not placed
cases.why: Z1, with no link, is handed a held point and is still not placed, since a node with no link is placed only by a Pin: Z1 and Z2 are in unplaced, by id (steps 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: centres across held and pinned pieces
cases.why: Beside the wheel, a piece with a Pin (m, seven nodes), a piece on the ring (g, six), a piece with a held node (k, six) and a pair on the ring (z): centres is the main run's, then each piece's in the ring's order over every piece, held and pinned ones too, m, then g before k by their lowest nodes, then z (steps 11 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: the largest piece a lone node
cases.why: Six nodes and no link, three pinned: the main run keeps only the pinned nodes, c0, d0 and e0 on the Map; the main piece, a0, is one node and not placed, and its centre is left out of centres; a0, b0 and f0 are in unplaced (steps 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: a piece held beyond its Pin's box
cases.why: P03 alone is handed a held point 770 rests out on x, and the main run holds none of it; P03's piece's run holds P03 there and P00 at its Pin, 773 rests apart: each run checks the box on what it holds, its Pins too, so that run refuses and the call with it, held-box (step 10; Refused).

cases.name: pieces: a pinned centre of its piece
cases.why: A wheel h00 to h06 beside the main wheel, its hub h00 pinned: the piece's run holds h00 at its Pin and makes it the piece's centre, so h01 to h06 stand with h00 and name it as their group, and h00 answers as a pinned centre of the main shape does, how map, group its own id, part null (steps 10 and 12).

cases.name: pieces: a frame held far from its piece
cases.why: W01, W05 and W09, on the first map, are held together where a frame agrees, 834 rests out on x from W02 and W03, held at their own earlier points: a pinned node's held value counts in the main run's box, since the frame puts the plate where those values say, so the box is wider than HELD_BOX and the call is refused, held-box, before the plate is placed (H1; Refused); the same frame 667 rests out is answered.

cases.name: refused: a box too wide and a bad heldUnit
cases.why: b1 and b2, of the main piece, held 46,081 units apart on x, and heldUnit -1: heldUnit is read with the shape of held, before anything runs, and the box only in each run, so the call is refused with held-unit, not held-box (Refused).

cases.name: held: no node, and held points wider than the box
cases.why: No node, and x and y held 46,081 units apart on x: neither is a node, so the one run holds neither, and the call is answered with nothing placed (step 10; Refused).

cases.name: held: a place passed over because it is near
cases.why: The earlier answer is handed back whole and f0, new, hangs from b5 beside f1: f1 is held at its earlier point, place 0 of b5's fan, and stands there, so place 0 is near it and f0, first in id order, passes it over and takes place 1; without f1 held, f0 takes place 0 (H6, what hangs); and under the pieces, q1 and q2 are laid out round their held points and not moved (step 10), and s1 and s2 are not placed (step 12).

cases.name: held: a point 1e-7 from a moving element's start (the push's floor)
cases.why: A wheel of six round h, h held at (0, 0, 0), and z, linked to n3 alone, held 1e-7 to the side of where n1 starts (step 7): z hangs outside the body, so it is kept as a fixed mover that pushes (H5), and at step 0 n1 and z are 1e-7 apart, so d is max(sqrt(d2), 0.000001) = 0.000001 (step 8, the push).

cases.name: pieces: a held answer fed back whole
cases.why: The answer of the all-in-one case handed back whole as held points: every placed node stands at the same point, the pinned ones at their Pins, and every piece, now held, is not moved (step 10; H5; H6, kept).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-a-map-that-places-all
unplaced.why: The fifteen-element graph of the cases, and a Map whose Pins stand for every element of it: nothing is unplaced (unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-one-element-more
unplaced.why: That graph with b9 added since the Map was saved, linked to b8 and b2: b9 is the one element the Map does not place (unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-a-placed-id-that-is-no-node
unplaced.why: Every element placed but s2, and zz, an id that is no node: s2 is unplaced, and zz is no part of the answer, which lists nodes only (unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-a-member-of-placed-that-is-no-id
unplaced.why: The graph with a node whose id is "7", linked to b1, and placed holding null, "" and the number 7 beside every other id: a member that is not a non-empty string names no element, and the number 7 is not the id "7", so "7" is unplaced (unplaced: placed is a list or a set).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-a-node-with-no-link-and-a-node-off-the-main-piece
unplaced.why: The Map places the main piece; q1 and q2 are a piece of their own and s1 and s2 have no link, and the Map holds no Pin for any of the four, so all four are unplaced, though the method places q1 and q2 on the ring (unplaced; steps 10 and 11).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-map-space-nodes-are-nodes
unplaced.why: A graph handed in with a Map, a Pin, a Marker and a Zone as nodes: every node counts whatever its type, so the four are unplaced (a tool that makes its graph as Which graph says leaves Map, Pin and Marker out of what it hands in) (Which graph; unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-ids-past-the-first-plane
unplaced.why: Two ids that differ in their second character, U+FF21 and U+10000, handed in the other order and neither placed: the answer is in code point order, where UTF-16 units (U+10000 is D800 DC00) would reverse them (unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-the-answer-by-id
unplaced.why: Four nodes handed in neither in id order nor in its reverse, d4 placed: the answer is by id, a1, b2, c3, not in the order handed (unplaced).

unplaced.name: by-links-3d-the-method-s-own-list
unplaced.why: The nodes of the case with a pinned lone node beside an unpinned one and the Map its answer makes, with a Pin for every placed node: that reading of the Map is the answer's own unplaced, L2 (unplaced; step 12).
